property: The BGP protocol family is revised to support classless IP-prefix reachability and route/AS-path aggregation while retaining the inter-AS path-vector/policy role.

date_or_range.notes: BGP-3 is documented in RFC 1267; RFC 1771 identifies itself as BGP-4 and describes the earlier versions explicitly.

sources.locator: title page, protocol version and appendix/version history
sources.supports: identity of BGP-3 and its place after RFC 1163/BGP-2

sources.locator: RFC 1771, Section 2 and appendices describing BGP-4/version changes
sources.supports: BGP-4 identity, classless prefixes, route aggregation, AS-path aggregation and BGP-1/2/3/4 naming
CIDR requirement for arbitrary network+mask routes, longest-match behavior and route aggregation
sources.notes: Shows that the classless transformation belongs to a broader address/routing-scaling lineage, not only to BGP's internal history.

negative_claims: This edge does not claim that BGP-4 invented CIDR; CIDR requirements were developed in a related address-allocation/interdomain-routing standards lineage.
This edge does not claim that publication of RFC 1771 instantly eliminated every BGP-3 session in production.
This edge does not imply that all BGP-3 encodings or policy semantics survived unchanged.
open_questions: Recover the first production BGP-4 deployments and their dates.
Identify exact Cisco, NSFNET/ANS, gated and other software releases implementing BGP-4.
Recover BGP-3/BGP-4 interoperability and version-negotiation incident reports.
Find early BGP-4 routing-table dumps demonstrating prefix aggregation in operational use.
Build a field-by-field UPDATE/path-attribute diff between RFC 1267 and RFC 1771.
notes: Reference example of a protocol revision whose defining change intersects another standards genealogy (CIDR).
